_doc: FALCON dating cabinet (#40, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #46). The metal-stem/screw-bowl system pipe: created 1936 by US engineer Kenly Bugg; George Hunt took over production+marketing 1949 (6M sold in the US by 1954); ENGLAND production from 1961; US (Chicago) production STOPPED 1968 -> the USA/England COM split is the spine. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Falcon.json (+ K.A. Worth's book 'Back From The Ashes' referenced = BUY-LIST candidate).

history_anchors._doc: 1936: Kenly Bugg (American engineer) creates the Falcon — metal stem, humidome moisture trap, screw-on interchangeable briar bowls. WWII limits production. 1949: George Hunt (G.L. Hunt) takes over; by 1954 six million sold in the USA. 1961: production starts in ENGLAND ('the' English pipe of its era). 1964: ALCO launched. 1967: BRENTFORD launched (withdrawn 1979). 1968: US Chicago production STOPS -> all Falcons after = English. 1977: FALCON INTERNATIONAL introduced (removable mouthpiece + filter). Today: BPM International (UK), falconpipes.co.uk.

brand_marks.physical: Aluminium stem + humidome; interchangeable screw bowls (bowls date poorly — swapped freely; DATE THE STEM, not the bowl). Straight/bent stems; Shillelagh twisted-stem variant (c.1968 example known).

line_years._notes: brentford: launched 1967, withdrawn 1979 = a CLOSED window (strong). alco: 1964 floor, end undocumented. international: 1977 floor (removable mouthpiece + filter = its tells).

table.label: Falcon brand window 1936+ (WWII production limited; the 1949-54 Hunt boom = the US mass era)

channels_future.worth_book: K.A. Worth, 'Back From The Ashes: G.L. Hunt and the Falcon Pipe' (2008) = the definitive history -> BUY LIST (would refine stem-stamp eras).
channels_future.bowl_traps: Bowls interchange freely across decades — never date a Falcon by its bowl.
channels_future.shillelagh: Twisted-stem Shillelagh c.1968 — single dated example, unencoded.
